dedupe_keys.name: kostra dwd 2020 gridded heavy rainfall depths by duration and return period for germany deutscher wetterdienst

description: KOSTRA-DWD (coordinated heavy precipitation regionalisation and evaluation of the Deutscher Wetterdienst) gives gridded precipitation depths and intensities for Germany as a function of rainfall duration and return period. DWD has produced it for more than 30 years; after KOSTRA-DWD-2000 (data 1951-2000), KOSTRA-DWD-2010 and its 2017 revision 2010R, the method was revised in the MUNSTAR project between 2018 and 2022, and since 1 January 2023 the valid edition is KOSTRA-DWD-2020, based on 1951-2020. Coverage: precipitation depths (mm) and rain intensities (litres per second per hectare) for 22 standard durations from 5 minutes to 7 days and return periods from 1 to 100 years, on a Germany-wide grid of cells of about 25 square kilometres. Format and access: free and without use restrictions on the DWD Climate Data Center open data server, with data tables (tab), ASCII grids with an Excel file of geographic reference values (asc) and GIS-ready vector data with class and colour schemes for nine return periods (gis); the 2010R edition is still in the same folder. Site-specific rainfall tables are sold by DWD on request. Licence: free of charge and without use restrictions under the German geodata access law, as stated by DWD. Caveats: the grids are regionalised values, not station statistics; the application guide and method reports (PDF) were not read. Simulation uses: design rainfall for sizing sewer networks, treatment plants, pumping stations, retention basins, drainage and infiltration systems, and for rating the return period of observed storms after damage events. Related records: the BKG heavy rainfall hazard map (data-bkg-germany-heavy-rainfall-hazard-map) shows where heavy rain causes surface flooding in Germany.
